description.narrative: The most significant expected Project-level outcome is increased access to finance MSMEs and increased access to climate finance including green buildings and circular economy. Beyond this outcome, IFC anticipates the Project will promote greater market sustainability as IFC anticipates that the investment will lead to an increase in climate finance throughout the Guatemalan financial sector.

The proposed project consists of an up to US$230 million financing package for Banco de America Central, S.A. (BAC Gt or the Bank) in Guatemala, composed of: (i) an up to US$200 million senior unsecured loan for IFCs own account (IFC A Loan); and (ii) a Global Trade Finance Program (GTFP) line of up to US$30 million. The loan will have a 4-year tenor with a 1.5-year grace period and the proceeds will be used to support the growth of the Bank's climate-smart assets (including green buildings and circular economy) and micro, small and medium-sized enterprises (MSME) loan portfolio. The trade line will support the Banks short-term trade finance transactions by offering confirming banks partial or full guarantees to cover payment risk of the Bank in Guatemala.
